newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs accept cut in ACP share of banana market.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs accept cut in ACP share of banana market.

text.p: The European Parliament adopted on Tuesday a European Commission proposal to cut the share of the European Union banana market allotted to the EU member states' former colonies.

Euro-MPs approved the draft regulation -- COM(96)82 -- even though Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler had told parliament's agriculture committee he would not accept the key amendments they wanted to the text.

Since the Commission was obliged to consult the parliament over the regulation but was not obliged to heed its amendments, Euro-MPs eventually decided imperfect legislation was better than none, a parliament official told Reuters.
The regulation increases from 2.2 million to 2.553 million tonnes the overall tariff quota, to account for the accession to the EU of Austria, Finland and Sweden.
At the same time, it raises from 66.5 to 70.5 percent the share of the EU market allotted to suppliers for imports of "dollar" bananas from Latin America-- mainly U.S.- based multinationals.

The extra percentage is to be found by cutting from 30 percent to 26 percent the share of the tariff quota allotted to traditional suppliers of bananas from Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific (ACP states).

In its report on the proposal, drafted by Italian Union for Europe Euro-MP Giacomo Santini, parliament complained the cut in the ACP market share ran counter to the EU's commitment to its former colonies under the EU-ACP Lome Convention.

By way of protest, Euro-MPs adopted amendments to the regulation which reinstated the ACP states' 30 percent share and provided for an overall tariff quota increase of only 100,000 tonnes (to 2.3 million tonnes).

"The 30 percent tariff quota volume amounts to the minimum compensation required (by the ACP states) to guarantee their survival and offer any sort of prospects for the future," Santini's report stressed.
The proposal now goes to the Council of Ministers for final approval.
